affiliations_and_recognitions: Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports (MYAS), Government of India
origin_story: During an international visit to Seoul, South Korea in 2014 for a Taekwondo championship, Jaspreet Singh Dhaliwal witnessed the sport of Boccia and the profound transformative impact it held for individuals with the most severe physical impairments (such as quadriplegia, advanced cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, and severe spinal cord trauma). Determined to introduce this life-altering precision sport to India, he returned and spent two years laying institutional groundwork, founding the Para Boccia Sports Welfare Society in 2016. What began as a passionate grassroots initiative has evolved into the recognized Boccia Sports Federation of India (BSFI), boasting affiliated state associations across India, regular national championships, and internationally ranked athletes on the World Boccia podium.

technology_and_equipment_innovations.title: Indigenous BC3 Assistive Boccia Ramp Initiative
technology_and_equipment_innovations.description: BC3 athletes have severe physical impairments in all four limbs and lack the manual strength or motor control to throw balls with their hands. They compete using an assistive ramp and a head/mouth pointer operated with a sports assistant. High-end international ramps typically cost thousands of euros, creating an insurmountable barrier for Indian athletes from humble backgrounds. Under Jaspreet Singh Dhaliwal's proactive leadership, BSFI partnered with ICMR and India's premier engineering institute, IIT Madras, to design, test, and manufacture precision-engineered, cost-effective indigenous Boccia ramps. This landmark development made the highest tier of the sport radically accessible to Indian athletes.
milestones: Official demonstration and review at ICMR Headquarters, New Delhi (Sep 2026).
Field testing and validation during National Coaching Camps in IAMD, Solan (Aug 2026).
Full compliance with World Boccia equipment regulations and dimensional tolerances.

international_milestones.significance: India's historic debut in Boccia at the Asian Para Games.
First major Middle-Eastern international exposure for Indian contingent.
Jaspreet Singh Dhaliwal served as Deputy Chef de Mission.

Historic 6-medal sweep by the Indian Boccia team led by BSFI President Jaspreet Singh Dhaliwal. Included India's first-ever individual international Boccia medal (Pooja Gupta, BC4 Bronze), Sachin Chamaria (BC3 Gold), and Jatin Kushwaha & Pooja Gupta (BC4 Pairs Silver).
BSFI President Jaspreet Singh Dhaliwal and Chairman Ashok Bedi represented India at the global governing body summit, advancing India's hosting rights and bilateral development.
Contingent of 6 Indian athletes competing across BC1, BC2, and BC3 categories.
Expansion of India's World Boccia circuit participation.
